title: Talking about a movie
why: With all the past tenses and the conditional under their belt, the learner can talk about culture: this lesson gives the phrases for introducing a movie (trata de, está ambientada en), summarizing it in the narrative present and giving a nuanced opinion. It opens the unit “Culture and leisure,” before reading a newspaper article and idiomatic expressions.

¿De qué trata? Introducing a movie

To introduce a movie, Spanish has a few ready-made phrases that are easy to reuse:

SpanishEnglish
La película trata de una familia que…The movie is about a family that…
Cuenta la historia de un hombre que…It tells the story of a man who…
Está ambientada en Sevilla, en los años cincuenta.It's set in Seville, in the fifties.
El protagonista es un profesor jubilado.The main character is a retired teacher.
Es la primera película de una directora gallega.It's the first movie by a Galician director.

Careful: película is feminine, so everything agrees in the feminine: está ambientada, la recomiendo, me ha parecido preciosa. Among friends, people also ask: ¿De qué va la película? (What's it about?)

Genres

una comedia, un drama, una película de terror, una película de ciencia ficción, una película de dibujos animados, una película de aventuras, un documental, un thriller.

Tricky movie words

  • el argumento: the plot, the story (not an “argument,” which is una discusión).
  • el guion: the script; el guionista, la guionista: the screenwriter.
  • la banda sonora: the soundtrack, the movie's music.
  • rodar: to shoot a movie; el rodaje: the shoot, the filming.
  • estrenarse: to come out, to be released; el estreno: the release, the premiere.
  • el actor, la actriz, plural las actrices (z becomes c).

Spanish cinema has its own awards, the Goyas, handed out every winter. Argentine and Mexican cinema are also very lively: when you watch them, you'll hear ustedes instead of vosotros.

", "

Summarizing a story in the present

As in English, you summarize a movie in the present: it's the narrative present. To link the stages, reuse the storytelling connectors: al principio, un día, entonces, mientras tanto, poco a poco, al final.

An example: “El verano de las cartas”

Here's the summary of an imaginary movie, written for this lesson:

«El verano de las cartas» está ambientada en un pueblo de Asturias en los años sesenta.“The Summer of the Letters” is set in a village in Asturias in the sixties.
La protagonista es Inés, una chica de dieciséis años que sueña con ser fotógrafa.The main character is Inés, a sixteen-year-old girl who dreams of being a photographer.
Un día, encuentra en casa una caja con cartas de su abuela, que nunca había hablado de su juventud.One day, she finds a box of letters at home from her grandmother, who had never talked about her youth.
Poco a poco, Inés descubre que su abuela vivió en Buenos Aires y que tuvo una vida muy diferente.Little by little, Inés discovers that her grandmother lived in Buenos Aires and had a very different life.
Mientras tanto, tiene que decidir si se queda en el pueblo o si se va a estudiar a Madrid.Meanwhile, she has to decide whether to stay in the village or go to Madrid to study.

The present is used for the main story, but what happened earlier stays in the past (vivió, había hablado), just as in English.

To avoid spoiling the surprise: No te cuento el final. (I won't tell you the ending.) In Spain, people also say hacer spoiler or, more colorfully, destripar el final (literally “to gut the ending”).

", "

Giving your opinion

For a movie you've just seen, the pretérito perfecto is natural in Spain: ¿Qué te ha parecido? For a movie you saw a long time ago, switch to the indefinido: La vi el año pasado y me encantó.

To say…Spanish
your overall impressionMe ha parecido muy original. / Me ha encantado. / No me ha gustado nada.
the best and the worstLo mejor es la banda sonora. / Lo peor es el final.
that it hooks youEngancha desde el principio.
that it's boring (informal)Es un rollo. / Se me ha hecho larguísima.
that you recommend itTe la recomiendo. / No te la recomiendo.

Parecer works like gustar: me ha parecido + adjective, and the adjective agrees with what you're judging: La película me ha parecido lenta, Los actores me han parecido geniales. Se me ha hecho larguísima (“it felt endless to me”) is a set expression.

Adjectives for judging

emocionante (exciting, moving), divertida (funny, fun), aburrida (boring), lenta (slow), sorprendente (surprising), previsible (predictable), preciosa (beautiful), original.

In Spain, most foreign movies are dubbed (doblados). If you prefer the actors' real voices, look for showings in versión original, often with subtítulos: they're marked VOSE, original version with Spanish subtitles.
